## `src/lib.rs`

### enum `Scope`

Where a secret lives (`docs/byo-credentials.md` §4.2) — a **third kind of scope**, not a reserved project id: `adi-app` keeps node passwords in a pseudo-project called `fleet-nodes` (`adi-app/src/viewer.rs:27`), which works only because nothing resolves that scope into a run. A user scope exists *to be* resolved into runs, so `User`'s id must never be mistaken for a `Project` id even though both pass the same filesystem-name check (`validate_project`).

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Scope<'a> {
    Global,
    Project(&'a str),
    User(&'a str),
}
```

### struct `Secrets`

The secrets store: sets, reads, and resolves per-scope encrypted secrets under the `secrets` module dir. Cheap to clone; all state is on disk.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Secrets {
    config: Config,
}
```

## `src/secret.rs`

### struct `Manifest`

A secret's on-disk manifest: the encrypted value plus metadata. The secret's **key name and scope are its file's location** (`global/<name>.toml` or `projects/<id>/<name>.toml`), not fields here — so this struct holds only ciphertext and descriptive data, never a plaintext value and never the name.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct Manifest {
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub nonce: String,
    pub ciphertext: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub created_at: u64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub updated_at: u64,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub oauth: Option<OAuthMeta>,
}
```

### struct `OAuthMeta`

The OAuth provenance of a secret's value, stored on disk. Everything here except the encrypted `refresh_*` is plaintext metadata; the access token lives in the manifest's own `ciphertext` (it's the secret's value).

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub(crate) struct OAuthMeta {
    pub provider: String,
    pub obtained_at: u64,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub expires_at: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub scope: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub refresh_nonce: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub refresh_ciphertext: Option<String>,
}
```

### struct `Secret`

A stored secret's **metadata** — its scope, name, description, and timestamps. It carries **no value**: the plaintext is only ever produced by an explicit `Secrets::reveal`, never as a field here, so listing or logging a `Secret` can't leak it. `Serialize` only — it is built from disk, never deserialized.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Secret {
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub project: Option<String>,
    pub name: String,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub description: Option<String>,
    pub created_at: u64,
    pub updated_at: u64,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub oauth: Option<OAuthInfo>,
}
```

### struct `OAuthInfo`

The non-secret view of a secret's OAuth provenance — safe to list/serialize. It reports the provider, the token lifetime, and whether a refresh token is held, but never a token value.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct OAuthInfo {
    pub provider: String,
    pub obtained_at: u64,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub expires_at: Option<u64>,
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
    pub scope: Option<String>,
    pub has_refresh: bool,
}
```

### struct `OAuthToken`

A freshly obtained OAuth token, handed to `Secrets::set_oauth` to store: the access token becomes the secret's (encrypted) value, the refresh token is encrypted separately, and the rest is metadata.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct OAuthToken {
    pub provider: String,
    pub access_token: String,
    pub refresh_token: Option<String>,
    pub expires_at: Option<u64>,
    pub scope: Option<String>,
}
```

## `src/settings.rs`

### enum `Missing`

What a turn does when it would use a user's value for a name and no live lease holds one (`docs/byo-credentials.md` §4.1, §10). Declared `Server < Wait < Fail` on purpose: deriving `Ord` off that order is what makes `effective_missing` "the stricter of the two" a one-line `max`, and it is also the order the spec states its reason in — `fail` ranks above `wait` because it is the one that also stops work piling up behind a missing value.

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "lowercase")]
pub enum Missing {
    #[default]
    Server,
    Wait,
    Fail,
}
```

### struct `UserSecretsPolicy`

`secrets/settings.toml`'s `[user_secrets]` table — the one switch that turns the whole feature on, and the one list that says which env-var names a user may ever replace.

```rust
}
```
